name: memblock_non_h
title: MemBlock non-H coverage target
description: Analyze Spike MemBlock-related coverage for NanHu-V5.1 AP while excluding H extension, stage2, and project-unsupported memory features.

coverage_focus.purpose: Analyze the NanHu-V5.1 AP MemBlock-related coverage slice: RV64 non-H, stage1 translation, scalar/FP/vector memory, LR/SC, word/doubleword AMO, CBO/CMO, and Svinval/SFence invalidation paths.
included_features: RV64 compressed integer and F/D memory instructions supported by NanHu-V5.1 AP
F/D floating-point scalar load/store forms supported by NanHu-V5.1 AP
RISC-V vector load/store forms supported by NanHu-V5.1 AP
LR/SC and word/doubleword AMO forms supported by NanHu-V5.1 AP
Zicbom/Zicbop/Zicboz CBO/CMO forms supported by NanHu-V5.1 AP
Svade A/D-bit behavior where source coverage exposes memory-visible paths
excluded_features: Zfh/Zfhmin/Zvfhmin/Zvh/Zfbfmin half-precision and BF16 memory forms
AIA, SMEPMP, pointer masking, and RAS paths
RV32-only compressed floating memory forms such as c.flw/c.fsw
Zicclsm misaligned-memory extension behavior as a positive in-scope feature
notes: This target defines the coverage slice only. The project implementation and coverage runner contract live in project_spec.
Project unsupported-feature filters are derived from specs/nanhu_v5_1_ap.json; keep target filters for target-specific scope only.
NanHu-V5.1 AP is treated as RV64 for this target, so RV32-only compressed floating memory entries are not in scope.
Zicclsm is NO in the project spec; misaligned-memory candidates are exception/priority/boundary checks, not positive Zicclsm behavior.
hyptest implementation still needs hyptest-workflow profile checks before writing cases.

scope_in: RV64 compressed integer and F/D memory instructions
Svade A/D-bit exception/permission behavior when memory-visible
scope_out: H extension instruction entries such as HLV/HSV/HLVX
guest page faults and trap_*_guest_page_fault targets
Zfh/Zfhmin/Zvfhmin/Zvh/Zfbfmin half-precision and BF16 memory targets
AIA, SMEPMP, pointer masking, and RAS targets
RV32-only compressed floating memory entries such as c_flw/c_flwsp/c_fsw/c_fswsp
analysis_notes: Prioritize branch/call gaps in shared paths such as riscv/mmu.cc, riscv/mmu.h, riscv/v_ext_macros.h, riscv/execute.cc, and riscv/triggers.cc over one-line instruction entry coverage.
Treat scalar/vector/atomic/CBO entries as entry evidence first; inspect shared MMU/vector/trigger/fault paths before claiming semantic coverage.

High-value MemBlock candidates usually need an observable memory/register/trap/CSR/vector oracle and should exercise a reusable behavior class such as alignment, boundary split, fault conversion, PMP/PMA/PBMT, trigger timing, TLB/PTE cache refresh, vector mask/vstart/fault-only-first, LR/SC reservation, AMO, or CBO gating.

For path-sensitive questions, do not claim a whole execution flow was covered just because each branch was covered in aggregate. Use single-case increment evidence or path markers; otherwise mark edge-covered-path-unknown.
Mark memtracer/log/device-specific paths as manual/special-run unless the default hyptest platform can observe them deterministically.
Do duplicate search by semantic terms as well as mnemonics before proposing implementation.

Apply the NanHu-V5.1 AP support matrix before proposing target gaps: Svinval/Svade/Svpbmt are in scope when memory-visible; Sv57/Svnapot/Svadu/H/Zacas/Zabha/Zfh/Q/Zawrs/Zicclsm-positive behavior are out of scope for this target.
For compressed memory, keep the RV64-supported C integer and F/D entries; do not treat RV32-only c.flw/c.fsw entries as missing AP coverage.
For misaligned-memory evidence, phrase candidates as trap priority, boundary split, or exception conversion behavior because Zicclsm is not supported by the project spec.

scenario_coverage.purpose: Find missing MemBlock non-H cross execution scenarios, not line/branch/call coverage numbers as goals.
scenario_axes: instruction/access class: fetch, scalar load/store, FP memory, vector load/store, LR/SC, AMO, CBO/CMO, fence/sfence/Svinval
privilege/profile/gate: M/S/U, enabled ISA/profile feature, default vs manual/special-run gate
address/translation/protection/device condition: bare/stage1 translation, TLB hit/miss/walk/refill/flush, alignment/boundary, PMP/PMA/PBMT, MMIO/device/responder

exception/fault/trigger/cache/vector/atomic subcondition: misaligned/page/access fault priority, trigger timing, cache error/NMI, vector mask/vstart/fault-only-first/indexed/whole, LR/SC reservation, AMO operation variant and aq/rl ordering
architectural observable: register value, memory bytes, trap cause/tval, CSR state, vector element/mask result, deterministic device/manual-run evidence
evidence_policy: Line/branch/call/entry coverage is supporting evidence, not the test intent.
Do not claim a MemBlock cross scenario is covered unless same-flow evidence ties instruction/access, translation/protection condition, subcondition, and observable together.
Use shared-path evidence in mmu.cc/mmu.h/v_ext_macros.h/execute.cc/triggers.cc to turn entry gaps into scenario gaps.
Derive scenario signatures from target scope, Spike source, .gcov, single-case deltas, or path-marker records; do not generate a blind Cartesian product.
Manual-only dimensions such as memtracer/log/device injection/cache error/NMI remain manual/special-run unless deterministic default-gate observability is proven.
Apply project-spec support before interpreting an entry gap: unsupported or RV32-only entries are out-of-scope even when Spike emits coverage files.
Treat Svinval/SFence invalidation as stage1 translation/TLB coverage, not as a separate blind instruction checklist.
priority_scenarios: stage1 translation with TLB/PTE cache state and visible trap or memory result
PMP/PMA/PBMT permission or memory-type decision on scalar/vector/atomic memory access
vector indexed/whole/mask/fault-only-first memory access with mask/vstart/progress observable
LR/SC and AMO reservation/compare/failure paths with memory/register observable
trigger/debug timing on load/store/fetch with trap or CSR observable
MMIO/device/responder and cache-error/NMI paths when only manual/special-run evidence is possible
Svinval/SFence invalidation followed by memory access with visible stale-vs-refreshed translation behavior
Svade A/D-bit disabled or permission behavior when source/gcov evidence exposes a memory-visible trap path

path_analysis.purpose: MemBlock path-aware coverage model for deciding whether a full execution flow, not only individual gcov edges, has run.
evidence_policy: Do not treat path_analysis as a complete path matrix or architecture specification.
Derive path signatures from Spike source and gcov evidence; do not invent combinations from a predeclared Cartesian product.
Use path_signature_fields only as a reporting checklist.
If all relevant edges are covered only in aggregate, mark edge-covered-path-unknown.
Use single-case increment evidence or per-instruction/access path markers before claiming same-flow path coverage.
path_signature_fields: address/translation/protection condition only when proven from source
exception/fault/trigger condition only when proven from source
vector/atomic condition only when proven from source
remaining uncertainty or reason path markers are needed

mem.access.fetch.meaning: Instruction fetch entered MemBlock/MMU access flow.

mem.access.scalar_load.meaning: Scalar or FP load entered MMU load flow.

mem.access.scalar_store.meaning: Scalar or FP store entered MMU store flow.

mem.access.amo.meaning: AMO/LR/SC entered the shared atomic memory flow.

mem.translate.tlb_hit.meaning: Access used an existing translation/cache entry.

mem.translate.tlb_miss_walk.meaning: Access missed the fast translation path and walked/refilled translation state.

mem.addr.misaligned.meaning: The access took the address-misaligned path.

mem.addr.cross_page.meaning: The access spans a page boundary or needs split/boundary handling.

mem.fault.page.meaning: The access raised an instruction/load/store page fault.

mem.fault.access.meaning: The access raised an instruction/load/store access fault.

mem.trigger.match.meaning: A memory-related trigger matched this access.

vec.mask.skip.meaning: A vector memory lane was skipped by mask.

vec.vstart.nonzero.meaning: Vector memory operation resumed from nonzero vstart.

vec.fault.partial.meaning: Vector memory operation made partial progress and then faulted.

mem.translate.invalidate.meaning: Stage1 translation invalidation path executed before or during a memory-visible translation scenario.

mem.pte.ad_check.meaning: Memory translation path reached PTE accessed/dirty-bit decision or Svade-related trap behavior.

required_practice: Use a tiny single-purpose case: one target memory/vector/atomic instruction plus minimal setup/check when possible.
Reset coverage counters or create a before .gcov snapshot, run only that case, regenerate .gcov, then compare before/after snapshots.
Use spike -l --log-commits --log=<file> when useful to prove the target guest instruction executed.
Treat increased line/branch/call counters as evidence for required path points, not as proof of arbitrary path combinations.
interpretation: If any must-pass line/branch/call remains zero, the full execution flow is confirmed-not-executed.
If counters increase but the run is not tiny/isolated or the Spike log does not confirm the target instruction, mark counter-increment-observed.
If all must-pass counters increase during a tiny single-purpose run and Spike log confirms the target instruction, mark single-case-increment-confirmed.
If counters were only covered in aggregate by a suite, mark edge-covered-path-unknown.
If internal path correlation cannot be proven by gcov increment plus log, mark needs-path-instrumentation and propose path markers.

marker_correlation_policy: Strong marker evidence requires JSON per-instruction/access records with pc+insn, seq, or access_id correlation fields.
JSON records without correlation fields and text fallback records are weak evidence only.
Marker sequence observation is evidence; the agent must still validate marker placement and architectural observable.

handoff_defaults.suggested_case_area: ai_test_cases or manual_test_cases/memblock after hyptest-workflow profile decision

memtracer/log paths.gate_note: manual/special-run unless the default platform exposes deterministic memtracer/log observables

MMIO/device paths.gate_note: manual/special-run unless a deterministic device/MMIO setup is available in default hyptest

micro cache error/NMI paths.gate_note: manual/special-run unless cache-error/NMI injection is available and deterministic in the selected platform
